status: Starter question set; not a claim of daily verified updates

questions.stem: A pregnant woman at 12 weeks has a previous pregnancy affected by a neural tube defect. Which folic acid regimen is most appropriate in a future planned pregnancy?
options: 5 mg daily from before conception until 12 weeks
5 mg daily only after the anomaly scan
No supplementation if diet is adequate
questions.rationale: A previous neural tube defect-affected pregnancy is a high-risk indication for high-dose folic acid before conception and through the first trimester. Confirm the exact current local guideline before prescribing.
questions.traps: Routine 400 microgram dosing is intended for lower-risk pregnancies; starting at 12 weeks misses the key neural tube closure window.

questions.stem: A haemodynamically unstable patient has a positive pregnancy test, abdominal pain and suspected ruptured ectopic pregnancy. What is the immediate priority?
options: Immediate resuscitation and urgent surgical assessment
questions.rationale: Maternal stabilisation and urgent operative assessment take precedence over serial investigations in suspected ruptured ectopic pregnancy.
questions.traps: Methotrexate and serial hCG are inappropriate for instability.

questions.stem: A woman with eclampsia has a generalised tonic-clonic seizure. Which drug is first-line to prevent recurrent seizures?
questions.rationale: Magnesium sulfate is first-line for prevention and treatment of recurrent eclamptic seizures, alongside stabilisation and delivery planning.
questions.traps: Other anticonvulsants are not preferred first-line in eclampsia.

questions.stem: Immediately after birth a woman has heavy vaginal bleeding and a boggy enlarged uterus. What is the most likely primary cause?
questions.rationale: A boggy uterus with immediate postpartum haemorrhage strongly suggests uterine atony; initiate the local PPH protocol immediately.
questions.traps: Trauma often causes bleeding despite a well-contracted uterus.

questions.stem: A 58-year-old woman presents with postmenopausal bleeding. What is the most important diagnosis to exclude?
questions.rationale: Postmenopausal bleeding requires assessment to exclude endometrial malignancy, even though benign causes are common.
questions.traps: Do not dismiss bleeding as atrophy without appropriate assessment.

questions.stem: A patient with a current breast cancer diagnosis requests contraception. Which option is generally most appropriate?
questions.rationale: A non-hormonal copper IUD is generally preferred where suitable in current breast cancer; assess individual contraindications.
questions.traps: Hormonal methods are generally contraindicated in current breast cancer.
